subject: botany
question_text: Which group of plants is called vascular cryptogams? Name the branch of Botany which deals with them.

verification.note: Sourced from the Telangana Junior Fastrack botany guide, Chapter 3 'Science of Plants' (book pp.5-6). The botany book prints NO star ranks and NO year citations, so stars=0 and appearances=[] record absence of signal, not measured frequency. Only ONE botany source is held — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper exists in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for botany: 'unverified' means never yet checkable against a second source, not checked-and-clean. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Vascular cryptogams
lines: They have vascular tissue (xylem and phloem)
but form no flowers and no seeds, so they
steps.why: The name itself decodes the group: 'vascular' because pteridophytes carry xylem and phloem, and 'cryptogams' because they reproduce by spores with no flowers or seeds.
common_mistakes: Answering bryophytes — bryophytes have no vascular tissue.
Writing only 'ferns' — the group name asked for is pteridophytes.
steps.memory_tip: Vascular rules out bryophytes; cryptogam (no seeds) rules out gymnosperms — pteridophytes are what remain.
steps.margin_note: Name the group, then one line on why the name fits.

steps.label: The branch
steps.why: The branch name is built from the group name: pterido- plus -logy gives pteridology.
common_mistakes: Leaving the branch out after naming the group — the question asks for both.
steps.margin_note: The boxed arrow line completes the answer.

insider_note: Group-and-branch questions repeat through this chapter (algae, fungi, bryophytes, pteridophytes, lichens); learn the five pairs as one table.
